title: Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri Reveals How He Manages Screen Time For His Children | Lifestyle News - News18
text: In today’s hyper-connected world, smartphones and gaming consoles heavily dominate children’s leisure time. Due to this, the debate over how much screen time is ‘too much’ has left many parents concerned. Interestingly, even the individuals behind the very platforms that shape our digital habits grapple with similar challenges. Recently, Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri discussed his personal approch to managing screen time for his children while appearing on the It’s Called Soccer! podcast. On his parenting approach to screen time, Mosseri shared that his children are not granted unlimited access and rather have to earn their 90 minutes daily. This ‘earned-access system’ emphasizes balance and responsibility, thus offering a more practical model for parents in the digital age. How it works? When asked how he deals with screen time when it comes to his children, Mosseri shared that they are “mostly into video games" and are required to “earn their time." “So, they have three half-an-hour sections a week where they do homework and then if they do all three of those, they earn their 90 minutes on the weekends," Mosseri said. He added that the kids have to start with none and then earn it. The Instagram CEO highlighted that he makes sure that he never takes it away from them. :But I don’t take it away because when I used to take it away they would really get super dysregulated and behave even worse," he said. Mosseri shared that he uses this method to instill discipline in them. However, he mentioned that these rules do not apply when they are travelling. “When really all barriers go out the window is on planes," he said. Mosseri’s approach seems practical as there is no strict ban when it comes to screen time. Instead of forbidding smartphones and gaming consoles, Mosseri encourages structured use, teaching balance and accountability. He further acknowledges the challenges to raise children in a world of endless scrolling and digital fatigue. Speaking at the Bloomberg Screentime conference a few months ago, Mosseri shared his three children are nine, seven and five years old. Mosseri’s views comes amid global debates over how much screen time is healthy for children. Amid concerns over mental health and attention spans, his approach highlights the importance of moderation. This encourages responsibility as children learn that screen time is more of a privilege rather than default. His idea reflects a growing parenting philosophy which remains focused on balance rather than strict bans.
